served.stem: A gas occupies 6 L at 1 atm and 127 °C. What is its volume at 4 atm and 27 °C?

answer.line: Four times the pressure shrinks the gas to 1/4; cooling to 300 K shrinks it to 3/4 more. 6 x 3/16 = 1.13 L.

steps: Convert to kelvin first: 127 degrees C is 400 K and 27 degrees C is 300 K. Gas laws only work in kelvin.
Push one change at a time. Pressure goes up 4 times, so the volume falls to 1/4.
Then the temperature falls from 400 K to 300 K, so the volume falls to 3/4 again. 6 L x 1/4 x 3/4 = 1.125 L, about 1.13 L.

choices.note: Both changes shrink the gas: 6 x 1/4 x 3/4.
This uses 400/300, as if cooling made the gas expand. Colder gas takes less room, so the factor is 3/4.
This multiplies by 4 instead of dividing. Squeezing a gas harder makes it smaller.
6 x 1/4 x 27/127 is about 0.319. A Celsius ratio means nothing to a gas; convert both temperatures to kelvin.
6 / 4 = 1.5 handles the pressure only. The temperature also dropped, which shrinks the gas a little more.

student.lockIt: Volume follows kelvin temperature and runs opposite to pressure. Apply each ratio in the direction the gas moves.
